findings.detail: GET https://tasknode.postfiat.org/api/tasks returns HTTP 200 with a 1,970-byte JSON body to an unauthenticated caller. The body exposes the internal eligibility policy (schema pf.task_node.network_task_eligibility.v1, requiresSignedInAccount, requiresLinkedPftWallet, requiresNetworkTaskOperatingBadge), the account gate list, dailyRewardCap 8, and per-wallet sync status. No per-user data leaked in the observed response (walletAddress null, requestCount 0, all record lists empty), so this is HIGH, not CRITICAL. The finding persists from the prior window: same endpoint, same shape, fresh re-probe.
findings.source_ref: outputs/api_probe.log: P-04 line; outputs/api_probe_raw.json: P-04 record (http 200, bytes 1970, tag UNAUTHENTICATED-JSON-READ)
findings.title: GET /api/tasks returns internal task state without authentication

findings.detail: submit, submit_multisigned, sign, sign_for, channel_authorize, and simulate are listed in the handler table as USER methods and are therefore reachable on the public endpoint. They were not called (SKIP, by design). There is no in-tree switch to disable sign/submit on a public node (negative search N-4: 0 hits). A caller who sends a private key to sign would hand it to the operator.
findings.source_ref: data/method_inventory.json: submit, submit_multisigned, sign, sign_for, channel_authorize, simulate rows (probe_class SKIP); outputs/negative_search.log: N-4 count 0
findings.title: State-changing and secret-bearing methods are reachable on the public RPC endpoint

findings.detail: Negative search N-2 finds 0 rate-limit/throttle hits in src/xrpld/rpc/. The only rate-limit terms tree-wide are overlay manifest rate limiting (ManifestRateLimitCapPolicy, uncapped for trusted peers) and ValidatorExclusionManager change throttling. The live probe saw 0 HTTP 429 in 68 calls + a 12-request burst (0.25 s apart) and 0 in a 5-request /api/tasks burst. The actual rate-limit threshold, if any exists outside the tree, is [UNSUPPORTED]: zero 429s is absence of a signal, not a measured limit.
findings.source_ref: outputs/negative_search.log: N-2 count 0 in rpc/, N-2b manifest/exclusion only; data/source_excerpts.json: E-17 (OverlayImpl.cpp:690-691)
findings.title: No public RPC rate limiting exists in the pinned tree

findings.detail: passwordUnrequiredOrSentCorrect returns true when admin_user/admin_password are empty, so a request from an admin IP is admin without any credential. isAdmin requires both the IP check AND the password check only when a password is set. Whether the public port has a password configured is not observable from outside ([UNSUPPORTED] U-02), but the code path means a misconfigured port exposes all 23 ADMIN methods to anyone on an admin net.
findings.title: Admin authentication degrades to an IP allowlist when no admin password is configured

findings.detail: Negative search N-1 finds 12 hits for admin_password/passwordUnrequired in src/xrpld/rpc/, all of them port/client setup and role-check plumbing; none is per-method. Any unauthenticated caller (GUEST role) can call any USER method, including state-changing ones (see R-01). The table's Condition enum describes ledger state, not mutability, so operators cannot tell from the table which methods mutate state.
findings.title: No per-method authentication beyond the table roles; all 51 USER methods are open to any caller

findings.detail: The table lists ledger as Role USER with NO_CONDITION, but LedgerHandler.cpp returns rpcNO_PERMISSION unless the caller has an unlimited role (ADMIN or IDENTIFIED). A USER caller requesting a full ledger or accounts gets rpcNO_PERMISSION (HTTP 401). The table understates the restriction; the real policy lives in the handler body.
findings.title: ledger full/accounts is gated by a second, in-handler check the table does not show

findings.detail: server_info (USER) returns build version 1.0.9, network id 2025, complete ledger range, hostid MUFF, the node public key, port list (2559 peer, 6005 ws, 50051 grpc), and peer counts (21). Useful for fingerprinting and targeting a specific build; no per-user data.
findings.source_ref: outputs/rpc_probe_raw.json: server_info record (build 1.0.9, hostid MUFF, peers 21)
findings.title: server_info leaks node fingerprinting data to anyone

findings.detail: manifest (USER) takes a master key and returns the full manifest (domain, ephemeral key, seq). Probed with the validator master key from the key-management pack: returns details (domain app.w.ai, seq 1). Public by design, but it lets anyone enumerate validator domains and sequence numbers.
findings.title: manifest returns any validator's manifest to any caller, enabling validator enumeration

findings.detail: transaction_entry returns notYetImplemented for a current-ledger query ('We don't support any transaction yet'). The method is dead in the table; callers cannot distinguish it from a working method without calling it.
findings.source_ref: data/source_excerpts.json: E-18 (TransactionEntry.cpp:54-60); outputs/rpc_probe_raw.json: transaction_entry record (error notYetImplemented)
findings.title: transaction_entry is listed in the table but not implemented

findings.detail: GET / and GET /api both return HTTP 200 with the same 1,141-byte SPA shell; only /robots.txt returns 404 (66 B). The routing fallback makes it impossible to distinguish a real route from a missing one by status code alone.
findings.title: Agent API serves the SPA shell for unknown paths, masking 404s

findings.detail: subscribe and unsubscribe over HTTP JSON-RPC return invalidParams (code 31). The table lists them as USER methods with NO_CONDITION and no transport note, so a reader of the table cannot tell they require a websocket.
findings.source_ref: outputs/rpc_probe_raw.json: subscribe record (invalidParams, code 31), unsubscribe record (invalidParams, code 31)
findings.title: subscribe/unsubscribe are websocket-only but listed as plain USER methods

findings.detail: Feature1.cpp returns rpcNO_PERMISSION for vetoing a feature without admin, and the feature list itself is rendered with getJson(feature, isAdmin), so admin-only fields are hidden from USER callers. This is the one place where the handler applies a finer-grained check than the table role.
findings.title: feature listing is role-aware (a working control)

findings.detail: exclusion_info returns error notEnabled (code 12): 'PF_AccountExclusion feature is not enabled'. This independently re-verifies the amendment-governance pack's live inventory (101 amendments, 64 enabled / 37 disabled, both PostFiat-specific amendments disabled).
findings.title: exclusion_info confirms PF_AccountExclusion is disabled (re-verifies the governance pack live)

findings.detail: All 68 RPC responses carry Server: Caddy and Content-Type: application/json; charset=UTF-8. The 403 responses additionally carry a second Server header, postfiat-json-rpc/postfiatd-1.0.9 (direct header inspection 2026-11-26T04:52:33Z). The 23 ADMIN refusals are HTTP 403 with an 11-byte plain-text body ('Forbidden'). The 403 is emitted by rippled itself: ServerHandler.cpp computes the role via requestRole and returns HTTP 403 when the role is FORBID (ServerHandler.cpp:752-757). The earlier hypothesis that a proxy does the refusing is wrong; the in-tree path is confirmed by negative search N-6 (5 hits, all in ServerHandler.cpp).
findings.source_ref: outputs/rpc_probe_raw.json: server_header Caddy on 68/68 records; 403 body 'Forbidden' (11 bytes); data/source_excerpts.json: E-11 (ServerHandler.cpp:752-757)
findings.title: The public RPC sits behind Caddy, but the observed 403s are rippled's own

findings.detail: All account_* probes against the genesis test account return actNotFound (code 19); ledger_entry returns entryNotFound (98); tx returns txnNotFound (29). The /api/tasks response has walletAddress null, requestCount 0, and all record lists empty. The unauthenticated read (A-01) exposes policy and configuration, not personal data.
findings.source_ref: outputs/rpc_probe_raw.json: error-result records (actNotFound 19, entryNotFound 98, txnNotFound 29); outputs/api_probe_raw.json: P-04 record (walletAddress null, requestCount 0)
findings.title: No per-user data leaked in any probe
